question: how many dated, route-typed pairs does the decision rule need before naming a winner tells a reader anything?
generative_assumption: the true model is one of the four and its declared parameters in this file are right. The simulation measures the decision rule's power under that assumption. It does not measure whether any of the four is true, and it cannot: a rule can be perfectly powered and still be fed a world none of the four describes.
what_the_number_is: the smallest pair count on the declared grid at which the stage-1 rule names the generating model decisively in at least the target share of replications, for every generating model -- so the binding cell is the hardest of the four to separate
what_the_number_is_not: a claim that any of the four models is true; a rule can be perfectly powered and still be fed a world none of the four describes
a measurement of this corpus: every input is a declared parameter of the instrument
independent of the grid: the floor is the first grid point that clears the target, so it is reported to the grid step and no finer
gate_is_not_part_of_what_is_measured: each replication is scored with the pair-count and effective-sample gates switched off, because the simulation is what sets them; measuring the rule with the gate in force would measure the previous run's placeholder
grid_provenance: Declared as 10 to 200 step 10 first. A run on that grid reached the 0.8 target for M2, M3 and M4 but not for M1, whose power topped out at 0.73 at the ceiling, so the correct output of that grid was `not_derivable_on_declared_grid` and it is reported in results/model_power_simulation.json as the reason the ceiling moved. Extending a grid ceiling can only raise the derived floor or leave it alone -- it never manufactures a smaller one -- which is why this extension is conservative rather than a second attempt at the same question. Shortening or re-centring it after a result would be the post-hoc move this field exists to expose.
derivation_rule: derived_minimum_pairs = max over the four generating models of the smallest grid pair count whose power reaches the declared target, and it is null unless every one of the four reaches it somewhere on the grid: a floor licensed where three of four truths resolve is a rule that goes silent on the fourth. derived_minimum_effective_samples = the 5th percentile (sorted, index ceil(0.05 * replications) - 1) of the Kish effective pair count over the replications of that binding cell

sensitivity.label: three_witnesses_per_work
sensitivity.change: witnesses_per_work 1 -> 3, so witness clusters add dependence on top of the work clusters

sensitivity.label: flat_background
sensitivity.change: M2's synthetic background made uniform over the five classes, so the null predicts less sharply

caveats: M1 and M3 predict a point mass at `identical` on a pair declaring no edges, because their likelihood is conditional on the declared edge multiset. Power against M2- and M4-generated sets is therefore driven by that collapse rather than by a comparison of distribution shapes, and those cells are easy. The binding cell is an edge-bearing comparison, which is why the derived floor is what it is.

the floor is reported to the grid step and no finer: a cell one step below the published floor may reach the target on a different seed, and the power column with its Monte Carlo standard error is published for every cell so a reader can see the noise rather than trust the crossing
a floor that lands on the grid ceiling is published as reached_only_at_the_grid_ceiling, and a model that reaches the target nowhere on the grid makes the floor null rather than partial
one witness per work is what the corpus is, and it is the weakest case for the effective-sample gate; the sensitivity scenario at three witnesses is published beside it rather than argued away
limitations: the simulation varies the pair count at a fixed cluster structure, so the two published floors are calibrated to each other and not independent; a pair set with a different work-per-pair ratio needs a rerun with that structure declared
power is a property of the decision rule under its own declared parameters, including the analyst-set background distribution M2 cannot yet supply
historical_conclusion: none asserted; this layer compares models against licence conditions, it does not settle a historical question
interpretation: a derived floor is a statement about this rule's resolution, not about the past. It changes only by rerunning this file, and the artifact records the parameters it was run under.
